\section[duḥkha]{\kn{ದುಃಖ} (duḥkha) — sadness}

\label{lesson:KA-C83-sadness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a headache, then the Kannada for rest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ದುಃಖ}}
\textbf{\kn{ದುಃಖ}} (\emph{duḥkha}) — \textquotedblleft{}sadness, sorrow\textquotedblright{}. The two small circles \textbf{\kn{ಃ}} after \textbf{\kn{ದು}} are the \emph{visarga}: a breath at the end of the syllable, \emph{duḥ-kha}.

It is the opposite of \textbf{\kn{ಸಂತೋಷ}} (\emph{santōṣa}), \textquotedblleft{}happiness\textquotedblright{}, which you met at the start.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The other side of santōṣa.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{duḥkha}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{duḥkha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{duḥkha} and then \emph{santōṣa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a headache, then the Kannada for rest, then say \emph{duḥkha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ದುಃಖ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sadness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cinte]{\kn{ಚಿಂತೆ} (cinte) — worry}

\label{lesson:KA-C83-worry}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for rest, then the Kannada for sadness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಚಿಂತೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಚಿಂತೆ}} (\emph{cinte}) — \textquotedblleft{}worry\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಚಿಂತೆ} \kn{ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ}} (\emph{cinte māḍabēḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}don't worry\textquotedblright{}. The ending \textbf{‑\kn{ಬೇಡಿ}} is \textbf{\kn{ಬೇಡ}}, \textquotedblleft{}don't want\textquotedblright{}, said politely.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A feeling, and a kind thing to say about it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cinte}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cinte}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cinte māḍabēḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for rest, then the Kannada for sadness, then say \emph{cinte} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಚಿಂತೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Worry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಭಯ}} (\emph{nanage bhaya}) — \textquotedblleft{}I am afraid\textquotedblright{}, again with the person in \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Fear, said with to-me like hunger and tiredness.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[kōpa]{\kn{ಕೋಪ} (kōpa) — anger}

\label{lesson:KA-C83-anger}

\textbf{\kn{ಕೋಪ} \kn{ಬೇಡ}} (\emph{kōpa bēḍa}) — \textquotedblleft{}no anger\textquotedblright{}, a gentle \textquotedblleft{}please don't be angry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A strong feeling, and a way to calm it.
\end{grammarlens}
